subject.title: [Feature]: Reusable gateway WebSocket client SDK package

question: Should OpenClaw publish and support a low-level `@openclaw/gateway-client` WebSocket SDK, or keep external clients on the higher-level SDK and documented Gateway RPC path for now?
rationale: Current main has private implementation groundwork, but publication would define new external auth, pairing, scope, reconnect, transport, token-storage, and support contracts that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep This As Direction Packet
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported low-level client boundary before publishing it or formally redirecting it to the higher-level SDK track.

options.title: Fold Into App SDK Track
options.body: Close or redirect this only after maintainers decide the public external-client contract is solely the higher-level SDK/Gateway RPC path and preserve the low-level requirements there.

options.title: Sponsor Gateway Client Publication
options.body: Move toward package publication with Node/browser support boundaries, install docs, security guidance, compatibility tests, and live Gateway pairing proof.

recommendation.title: Keep This As Direction Packet
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported low-level client boundary before publishing it or formally redirecting it to the higher-level SDK track.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest implemented boundary is the package extraction and host-wrapper design from the merged gateway-client package work.
